current_state.last_known_manifest_state: manifest.json and manifest.jsonl agreed before subsequent failed recovery attempts
current_state.known_risk: none — permissions restored (dirs 755, files 644, tools 755); snapshots hardened to 555/444 only

repeated_mistakes.description: Recursive chmod operations were applied with incorrect modes, removing directory execute permissions and causing Permission denied errors.
repeated_mistakes.remediation: Use an explicit target path and a per-class permission map. Directories require execute permission; do not use bare find . for repository-wide permission changes.

repeated_mistakes.description: A snapshot filename did not match the canonical SHA-256 hash of its JSON content.
repeated_mistakes.remediation: Run the session audit before committing and reject any filename/content hash mismatch.

repeated_mistakes.description: Operational artifacts were moved or retained inconsistently, causing repository noise and confusion between tracked and ignored files.
repeated_mistakes.remediation: Use explicit .gitignore rules and use git rm --cached when stopping tracking without deleting a file.

repeated_mistakes.description: Repeated one-off repair scripts increased artifact noise and introduced malformed or incomplete heredoc content.
repeated_mistakes.remediation: Use one validated recovery script at a time, write scripts outside the affected repository when possible, and inspect the complete file before execution.

repeated_mistakes.description: Recursive chmod via find executed from the repository root clobbered .git internals, froze Git, and removed hook executability.
repeated_mistakes.remediation: Never run bare find . permission operations. Exclude .git explicitly and preserve the repository root at mode 755.

repeated_mistakes.description: A malformed heredoc or pasted command produced incomplete script content; the M005 verification then failed with 'M005 entry not found'.
repeated_mistakes.remediation: Use a temporary file outside the repository, validate with bash -n or python3 -m py_compile, and inspect the generated file before running it.

hardening_recommendations.title: Scoped Permission Enforcement
hardening_recommendations.action: Apply permission changes only to the intended directory, never to the repository root or .git.

hardening_recommendations.title: Git Permission Baseline
hardening_recommendations.action: Keep .git directories at 755, ordinary .git files at 644, hooks that must execute at 755, and the repository root at 755.

hardening_recommendations.title: Manifest Synchronization
hardening_recommendations.action: Treat manifest.jsonl as authoritative and regenerate manifest.json only after confirming the output file is writable.

hardening_recommendations.title: Atomic Commit Guard
hardening_recommendations.action: Run audit_sessions.py from the pre-commit hook and abort commits on any audit failure.

recovery_sequence: Restore .git directories to 755 and .git files to 644.
Restore executable permissions only for intended hooks and tools.
Verify .git write access with a temporary write test.
Verify manifest.json is valid JSON and non-empty.

operator_notes: Do not use chmod -R or find . for repository permission changes.
Do not redirect directly over manifest.json until writability has been confirmed.
A successful echo after a failed command is not proof of success; use set -euo pipefail and test the actual output.
Do not move tracked files with mv alone; use git rm --cached when appropriate.
Keep recovery scripts outside the repository until they have passed syntax validation.
